analysis:
The PR changes documentation only. docs/provider/cli-reference.md changes the benchmark table at base/head line 519. It documents the new `--runtime-concurrency` and `--runtime-stagger` flags, visible at head lines 1145-1146. docs/reference/configuration.md adds two env-var rows at head lines 316-317, `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED` and `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY`. Both are default-on switches for Qwen MTP decode scheduling, and both are documented as not forwarded to LaunchAgents.

The changes touch no coordinator-provider protocol, attestation, App Attest authorization, key custody, prefix-cache storage, or fan-helper code. The affected assets and boundaries are A-001, TB-007, T-041 and T-053. None of them is altered, and the new env rows do not touch the prefix-cache gate (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE), the TTL or the HMAC lookup-tag derivation.

One point to check: the benchmark concurrency mode is documented as local diagnostic output (JSON to stdout). It is not a network surface. The documented `--runtime-concurrency` command says prefix caches stay off, consistent with the existing runtime-generation text.

I saw only the documentation; the underlying Swift code (MTPContractsV2.swift, RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark) is outside the supplied evidence. I therefore did not verify that the code matches the docs, such as the claimed 'not forwarded' behavior or that a benchmark never emits prompt content beyond the operator's own local prompt. Both claims are plausible but unverified. The unseen code and the doc accuracy are the open integration questions, not security regressions.

The docs also leave existing threat-model text valid. No new threat-model gap is introduced by this documentation.
